people.name: Sam Altman
people.bio_zh: OpenAI联合创始人兼首席执行官，曾领导创业加速器Y Combinator。他的公开输出把模型进展、算力建设、创业组织与社会变化连接起来，适合观察一线决策者如何形成长期判断，以及研究能力怎样转化为广泛使用的产品。
people.bio_en: Sam Altman is the co-founder and CEO of OpenAI and previously led Y Combinator. His public writing and interviews connect advances in models with infrastructure, startup strategy, and social change. He is useful to follow for understanding how a frontier laboratory allocates resources, develops products, and translates uncertain technical progress into an operating vision for a large organization.

比较技术能力进步与社会采用速度，检验他关于个人创造力和创业机会的判断。
ideas_en: Trace the relationship between compute, energy, financing, and model capabilities.
Compare technical progress with adoption speed and test his claims about entrepreneurship and individual agency.

people.bio_en: Greg Brockman is OpenAI’s co-founder and president and was previously Stripe’s chief technology officer. His experience spans engineering infrastructure, developer tools, large models, and deployment. His interviews offer a useful perspective on the organizational work between a research result and a usable product, including agent interfaces, reliability, and the changing relationship between human engineers and increasingly capable AI systems.

people.name: Ilya Sutskever
people.bio_zh: 深度学习研究者、OpenAI联合创始人及前首席科学家，现领导Safe Superintelligence。他的访谈较少，但常直接触及智能研究的基本问题：为什么模型能力不均衡、人类为何更善于泛化，以及规模扩张之外还有哪些关键研究方向。
people.bio_en: Ilya Sutskever is a deep learning researcher, co-founder and former chief scientist of OpenAI, and CEO of Safe Superintelligence. His relatively rare interviews focus on fundamental questions rather than product announcements. They are valuable for exploring why models generalize unevenly, what scaling does and does not explain, and how research taste shapes the search for more capable and dependable intelligence.

Founded SSI in 2024 and formally became CEO in 2025.
ideas_zh: 区分基准成绩与真实泛化能力，追问模型能力为何呈现不均衡。
理解预训练、研究创新和安全设计之间的关系，不把扩张规模视为唯一变量。
ideas_en: Distinguish benchmark performance from generalization and examine uneven model capabilities.
Explore the relationship between pretraining, research innovation, and safety beyond simple scaling.

people.name: Demis Hassabis
people.bio_zh: DeepMind联合创始人，研究经历连接游戏、神经科学与人工智能，因AlphaFold相关工作获2024年诺贝尔化学奖。他把通用智能视为推动科学发现的工具，是理解AI如何连接蛋白质研究、药物开发与更广泛科学问题的重要人物。
people.bio_en: Demis Hassabis co-founded DeepMind and helped lead its work from game-playing systems to scientific applications. His background connects computer science and cognitive neuroscience, and he shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold. His interviews are especially useful for exploring how general intelligence research can contribute to biology, drug discovery, and other scientific questions while confronting limitations in consistency and creativity.

Led teams behind AlphaGo and AlphaFold and founded Isomorphic Labs.
ideas_zh: 分辨解决单一科学问题的专门系统与通用智能路线之间的共通点和差异。
追踪从蛋白质结构预测到药物开发时，模型能力如何接受实验验证。
ideas_en: Compare specialized scientific systems with routes toward general intelligence.

people.bio_en: Andrej Karpathy is an AI researcher and educator known for explaining neural networks through concrete implementations. He was a founding member of OpenAI, directed AI at Tesla, and helped develop Stanford’s computer vision teaching. His writing and demonstrations bridge conceptual understanding and practical experimentation, making him useful to follow for changes in programming, personal software, and the way people learn with AI.

An early OpenAI member; returned in 2023–2024 to work on midtraining and synthetic data.

观察自然语言委托如何改变软件创造流程，以及哪些工作仍需人类判断。

people.name: Geoffrey Hinton
people.bio_zh: 深度学习的重要奠基者，长期研究神经网络、分布式表征和学习机制，曾在多伦多大学与Google工作。他的价值不仅在于技术史，也在于不断追问数字智能与生物智能的区别，以及理解能力提升后人类如何保持对系统行为的掌握。
people.bio_en: Geoffrey Hinton is a pioneering neural-network researcher whose work includes distributed representations, learning algorithms, and deep networks. He is an emeritus professor at the University of Toronto and previously worked at Google. His talks help connect the history of machine learning with fundamental questions about representation, biological and digital intelligence, and whether increasingly capable systems can remain understandable and controllable.
people.current_zh: 多伦多大学荣休杰出教授
people.current_en: Emeritus Distinguished Professor, University of Toronto
history_zh: 长期在多伦多大学研究神经网络与机器学习。
2013—2023年在Google兼职工作，曾任副总裁与工程院士。
history_en: Conducted long-running neural-network and machine-learning research at Toronto.
Worked part-time at Google from 2013 to 2023, becoming a Vice President and Engineering Fellow.
ideas_zh: 理解分布式表征为什么能让神经网络从数据中学习复杂结构。
比较数字智能的信息共享方式与生物学习机制，并思考控制问题。
ideas_en: Understand why distributed representations help networks learn complex structure.
Compare information sharing in digital intelligence with biological learning and examine control problems.

people.name: Yann LeCun

people.bio_en: Yann LeCun is a pioneering neural-network researcher and a joint recipient of the 2018 Turing Award. A longtime NYU professor and former leader of Meta’s AI research, he emphasizes self-supervised learning, world models, and planning. His interviews offer a clear alternative perspective on the limitations of language models and the architectural changes that might support more capable autonomous systems.
people.current_zh: AMI Labs执行主席、纽约大学Jacob T. Schwartz教授

2003年加入纽约大学，曾创办NYU数据科学中心。
history_en: Founded and led Facebook AI Research; later served as Meta’s Chief AI Scientist through 2025.
Joined NYU in 2003 and founded its Center for Data Science.
ideas_zh: 理解世界模型如何支持预测、规划和行动，以及它与逐词生成的区别。
把对现有语言模型的批评转成可检验的研究问题，比较不同智能路线。
ideas_en: Explore how world models support prediction, planning, and action.
Turn critiques of language models into testable research questions and compare alternative architectures.

people.name: Yoshua Bengio

people.bio_en: Yoshua Bengio is a pioneering deep learning researcher and a joint recipient of the 2018 Turing Award. Based in Montreal, he has helped build both research institutions and a broad community of machine-learning researchers. His recent work explores safer AI architectures, particularly systems designed to predict and understand without pursuing independent goals, alongside questions about scientific responsibility and the incentives shaping frontier development.

研究安全设计能否进入学习目标和模型结构，而不只依赖部署后的限制。
ideas_en: Compare systems that predict and understand with agents that autonomously pursue goals.
Examine whether safety can be built into learning objectives and architectures, beyond deployment controls.

people.name: Richard Sutton
people.bio_zh: Richard Sutton是强化学习的重要奠基者，与Andrew Barto共同获2024年图灵奖，也是《苦涩的教训》的作者。他持续追问智能如何从经验中学习，适合用来检视大模型路线、持续学习与人为知识之间的关系。
people.bio_en: Richard Sutton is a pioneer of reinforcement learning and a joint recipient, with Andrew Barto, of the 2024 Turing Award. He is also the author of The Bitter Lesson. His work asks how agents can learn and plan from experience. His interviews are especially valuable for challenging assumptions about language models, continual learning and the role of human knowledge in scalable intelligence.

history_zh: 与Andrew Barto合著强化学习领域的经典教材。
曾参与DeepMind Alberta，后与John Carmack在Keen Technologies合作。
history_en: Coauthored the foundational reinforcement-learning textbook with Andrew Barto.
Worked with DeepMind Alberta and later with John Carmack at Keen Technologies.
ideas_zh: 理解《苦涩的教训》对可扩展学习方法的要求，而不把它简化成只增加算力。
用持续学习和现实环境反馈，检验语言模型能否形成长期适应能力。
ideas_en: Read The Bitter Lesson as a case for scalable learning methods, beyond merely adding compute.
Use continual learning and environmental feedback to assess long-term adaptation in AI.

Earlier, he helped develop the poker systems Libratus and Pluribus and the Diplomacy-playing system CICERO. His discussions connect lessons from strategic games to test-time computation and agent collaboration, offering a concrete way to examine when additional thinking improves results and when it reaches practical limits.

people.bio_en: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein works across machine learning, neuroscience and statistical physics. He helped introduce diffusion models and has studied neural-network theory, learned optimizers and the behavior of large models. His essays and lectures are useful for connecting foundational research to changing scientific practice, especially how researchers should choose questions when increasingly capable AI systems alter the cost and pace of investigation.

At MIT and the Broad Institute, his group searches biological diversity for molecular systems that can be adapted into useful tools. His perspective connects discovery with engineering: editing DNA is one capability, while controlling RNA, delivering molecular machinery and choosing a tractable therapeutic problem require different solutions.

people.current_en: MIT professor and core member of the Broad Institute, researching genome engineering and programmable therapeutics.

参与开发 CRISPR-Cas9 哺乳动物编辑，并拓展 Cas12、Cas13 等分子工具。
history_en: Joined MIT and the Broad Institute in 2011, building a laboratory spanning neuroscience and genome engineering.
Helped develop mammalian CRISPR-Cas9 editing and expanded the toolbox with Cas12 and Cas13 systems.
ideas_zh: 怎样从自然界分子系统中识别可工程化的新能力。
为什么治疗效果取决于编辑、递送和疾病机制的共同约束。
ideas_en: How to recognize engineerable capabilities in naturally occurring molecular systems.
Why editing, delivery and disease biology jointly determine therapeutic feasibility.

推动多重基因编辑、基因组重编码与异种移植相关技术。

Advanced multiplex genome editing, genome recoding and technologies relevant to xenotransplantation.

Delivery, mutation coverage and clinical evidence remain important distinctions when following therapeutic progress.

people.bio_en: Lei Stanley Qi is a Stanford bioengineer who helped establish CRISPR interference and related gene-regulation technologies. His work uses catalytically inactive Cas proteins to target genomic locations without necessarily cutting DNA. That shift expands CRISPR into a platform for controlling expression, imaging genomes and modifying epigenetic states. His research provides a useful way to compare permanent sequence editing with other approaches to changing cellular behavior.

history_en: Trained in bioengineering at UC Berkeley and then began independent research at UCSF.
Joined Stanford in 2014 and developed CRISPRi, CRISPRa and epigenetic-editing technologies.
ideas_zh: 不切断 DNA 时，CRISPR 还能实现哪些干预。

people.bio_zh: 何川是化学生物学家，研究 RNA 与 DNA 修饰如何调控基因表达。其团队对可逆 RNA 甲基化的工作，拓展了人们对遗传信息调节层次的理解。这条研究路线特别适合观察一个基础机制如何带来新检测方法、新药靶点，以及农业和其他应用中的新问题。
people.bio_en: Chuan He is a chemical biologist studying how chemical modifications to RNA and DNA regulate gene expression. His laboratory helped establish reversible RNA methylation as an important layer of biological control. At the University of Chicago, his research combines chemistry, molecular biology and genomics. Following his work is useful for understanding how a newly identified regulatory mechanism creates both scientific questions and possible therapeutic or agricultural applications.
people.current_zh: 芝加哥大学 John T. Wilson 杰出服务教授；RNA 修饰与化学生物学研究者。
people.current_en: John T. Wilson Distinguished Service Professor at the University of Chicago, studying RNA modification and chemical biology.
history_zh: 在中国科学技术大学、MIT 与哈佛接受化学和化学生物学训练。
2002 年加入芝加哥大学，团队发现 RNA 去甲基化酶并推进可逆 RNA 修饰研究。
history_en: Trained in chemistry and chemical biology at USTC, MIT and Harvard.
Joined the University of Chicago in 2002; his group discovered an RNA demethylase and advanced reversible RNA-modification research.
ideas_zh: 新的调控层次怎样改变对疾病机制的解释。
从机制到靶点之间，还需要哪些因果证据。
ideas_en: How a new regulatory layer changes explanations of disease mechanisms.
What causal evidence is needed to turn a mechanism into a therapeutic target.

people.name: David Baker
people.bio_zh: David Baker 长期研究蛋白质结构与设计，其团队把计算建模、进化思路和生成式 AI 用于创造自然界没有的新蛋白。2024 年他获诺贝尔化学奖。值得追踪的主线是从预测转向设计：把一个医疗、材料或环境问题，转化成可制造并可测试的分子功能。
people.bio_en: David Baker is a biochemist and protein-design researcher at the University of Washington. His laboratory developed Rosetta and later methods that use modern machine learning to create proteins with new structures and functions. He received the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design. His work provides a bridge from abstract molecular design to applications in medicine, materials, sensing and environmental chemistry.
people.current_zh: 华盛顿大学生物化学教授、Institute for Protein Design 主任。
people.current_en: Professor of biochemistry at the University of Washington and director of the Institute for Protein Design.
history_zh: 开发 Rosetta 等计算方法，研究蛋白质折叠并推进从头设计。
因计算蛋白质设计获 2024 年诺贝尔化学奖。
history_en: Developed Rosetta and related computational approaches to folding and de novo protein design.
Received the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design.
ideas_zh: 怎样把实际需求写成蛋白质可实现的结构与功能约束。
预测准确、实验有效与能够规模化生产有何差别。
ideas_en: How to express practical needs as structural and functional constraints for proteins.
How predictive accuracy differs from experimental effectiveness and scalable production.

people.name: John Jumper
people.bio_zh: John Jumper 是 AlphaFold 核心研究者，因蛋白质结构预测获诺贝尔化学奖。他的背景横跨物理、化学与机器学习，适合帮助理解 AI 科研的问题选择、模型与领域知识的结合，以及结构预测成功后仍待解决的实验和药物开发问题。
people.bio_en: John Jumper is a scientist best known for leading the development of AlphaFold at Google DeepMind. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis for protein-structure prediction. His training spans physics and chemistry, making his perspective useful for understanding how machine learning and scientific knowledge interact. In June 2026, he announced a move to Anthropic after his work on AlphaFold.
people.current_zh: AlphaFold 核心研究者；2026 年 6 月宣布离开 DeepMind、转往 Anthropic。
people.current_en: AlphaFold researcher; announced in June 2026 that he would leave DeepMind for Anthropic.
history_zh: 在芝加哥大学完成化学博士训练，后在 DeepMind 参与并领导 AlphaFold 研究。
2024 年获诺贝尔化学奖；2026 年 6 月宣布离开 DeepMind 转往 Anthropic。
history_en: Completed doctoral training in chemistry at the University of Chicago before joining and leading AlphaFold research at DeepMind.
Received the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize and announced his move from DeepMind to Anthropic in June 2026.
ideas_zh: 科学问题的表示方式为何能决定 AI 方法是否有效。
结构预测解决了什么，又为何不直接等于药物发现。
ideas_en: Why the representation of a scientific problem can determine whether an AI method works.
What structure prediction solves, and why it does not by itself solve drug discovery.

people.name: Patrick Hsu
people.bio_zh: Patrick Hsu 研究基因组工程与机器学习，也是 Arc Institute 联合创始人。他参与早期 CRISPR 工具开发，并推动基因组基础模型和可编程重组系统。访谈适合关注科研品味、团队组织，以及如何把 AI 预测接回持续产生新数据的实验体系。
people.bio_en: Patrick Hsu works at the intersection of genome engineering and machine learning. A co-founder of Arc Institute and Stanford faculty member, he contributed to early CRISPR technologies and now develops approaches including genome foundation models and programmable DNA recombination. His interviews connect scientific taste with institutional design: how to select consequential questions, assemble complementary teams and create feedback between computational predictions and biological experiments.
people.current_zh: Arc Institute 联合创始人、斯坦福大学病理学助理教授及 Sarafan ChEM-H Faculty Fellow。
people.current_en: Co-founder of Arc Institute, assistant professor of pathology and Sarafan ChEM-H Faculty Fellow at Stanford.
history_zh: 在哈佛及 Broad 接受博士训练，参与早期 CRISPR-Cas9 基因组编辑研究。
联合创立 Arc Institute；团队推进 Evo 基因组模型与可编程 DNA 重组技术。
history_en: Completed doctoral training at Harvard and the Broad Institute, contributing to early CRISPR-Cas9 editing research.
Co-founded Arc Institute; his group developed Evo genome models and programmable DNA-recombination technologies.
ideas_zh: 如何形成科研品味，选择会改变工具和研究范式的问题。
模型、实验与研究组织如何形成持续学习的循环。
ideas_en: How to develop scientific taste and identify questions that change research tools and practices.
How models, experiments and research organizations can form a sustained learning cycle.

people.name: Aviv Regev
people.bio_zh: Aviv Regev 是计算生物学与单细胞研究的重要推动者，关注细胞类型、状态和调控网络如何构成疾病。她从学术研究走向大型药企研发管理，能够把细胞图谱、数据质量和药物决策放在同一框架讨论，适合学习如何从大规模观察走向可验证、可干预的机制。
people.bio_en: Aviv Regev is a computational biologist whose work helped establish modern single-cell genomics and the Human Cell Atlas. She now leads research and early development at Genentech after a career at MIT and the Broad Institute. Her perspective connects cellular maps with intervention: which differences matter, how experimental data should be generated and how biological understanding can guide choices in drug discovery.
people.current_zh: Genentech 研究与早期开发负责人、执行副总裁。
people.current_en: Head and executive vice president of Genentech Research and Early Development.
history_zh: 曾任 MIT 生物学教授及 Broad Institute 教员主席，并创立 Klarman Cell Observatory。
参与发起 Human Cell Atlas，2020 年开始领导 Genentech 研究与早期开发。
history_en: Served as an MIT biology professor and Broad faculty chair, founding the Klarman Cell Observatory.
Co-founded the Human Cell Atlas and began leading Genentech research and early development in 2020.
ideas_zh: 细胞图谱如何变成对疾病状态与调控机制的理解。
研究数据的规模、质量和可干预性如何共同影响药物决策。
ideas_en: How cell atlases become explanations of disease states and regulatory mechanisms.
How data scale, quality and intervention relevance jointly shape drug-discovery decisions.

people.bio_en: Daphne Koller is a machine-learning researcher and founder of insitro. Previously a Stanford professor and co-founder of Coursera, she moved into biology through work at Calico and then built a company combining experimental biology with machine learning. Her perspective is useful for understanding why drug discovery depends on generating informative data, defining meaningful disease phenotypes and testing predictions rather than simply applying larger models.
people.current_zh: insitro 创始人兼 CEO；机器学习与药物发现研究者。
people.current_en: Founder and CEO of insitro, working at the intersection of machine learning and drug discovery.
history_zh: 曾任斯坦福大学计算机科学教授，并联合创办 Coursera。
曾任 Calico 首席计算官，随后创立 insitro。
history_en: Was a computer-science professor at Stanford and co-founded Coursera.
Served as chief computing officer at Calico before founding insitro.
ideas_zh: 为什么数据生成与实验设计是 AI 制药的核心能力。
怎样从疾病表型与预测相关性推进到可验证的药物假设。
ideas_en: Why data generation and experimental design are core capabilities in AI drug discovery.
How to move from disease phenotypes and predictive associations to testable drug hypotheses.

people.name: Carl June
people.bio_zh: Carl June 是 CAR-T 细胞治疗的关键推动者，带领研究把患者免疫细胞工程化后用于治疗癌症。他的经历横跨免疫学、临床试验与疗法转化，适合理解一项惊人的个案结果如何发展成可靠治疗，以及毒性、制造、成本和适用人群为何决定技术能走多远。
people.bio_en: Carl June is an immunologist whose team helped establish CAR-T cell therapy for cancer. At the University of Pennsylvania, his work connects the engineering of T cells with clinical testing and therapeutic development. His career is particularly useful for understanding how an experimental treatment progresses beyond a striking patient response. Safety, manufacturing, cost and the biology of different diseases all shape whether a therapy can reach more people.
people.current_zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学教授、细胞免疫治疗中心主任。
people.current_en: Professor at the University of Pennsylvania and director of the Center for Cellular Immunotherapies.
history_zh: 早期在军方医学与免疫学研究中接受训练，后在宾大开展细胞治疗研究。
团队推进 CAR-T 临床试验，并为首批获批 CAR-T 疗法奠定基础。
history_en: Trained in military medicine and immunology before developing cell therapies at Penn.
His team advanced clinical CAR-T studies that helped underpin the first approved CAR-T therapies.
ideas_zh: 单个患者的突破如何转变为可复制的临床证据。
细胞疗法的毒性、制造复杂度和成本如何影响普及。
ideas_en: How a breakthrough patient response becomes reproducible clinical evidence.
How toxicity, manufacturing complexity and cost shape access to cell therapy.

people.name: James P. Allison
people.bio_zh: James Allison 长期研究 T 细胞激活与抑制机制，推动了免疫检查点治疗，并获得 2018 年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。他的故事能帮助理解基础免疫学为何改变癌症治疗，也适合讨论研究者如何在反复质疑中辨别真正有价值的机制，以及为何不同患者反应差异巨大。
people.bio_en: James P. Allison is an immunologist whose work on T-cell regulation helped establish immune-checkpoint therapy for cancer. He shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Tasuku Honjo. Based at MD Anderson, he connects basic questions about immune activation with clinical treatment strategies. His story offers a concrete example of pursuing a disputed mechanism while using experiments to distinguish conviction from evidence.
people.current_zh: MD Anderson 免疫学研究者、James P. Allison Institute 主任。
people.current_en: Immunology researcher at MD Anderson and director of the James P. Allison Institute.
history_zh: 阐明 T 细胞信号调节的重要机制，并推动 CTLA-4 阻断治疗研究。
与本庶佑共同获得 2018 年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。
history_en: Clarified mechanisms of T-cell regulation and advanced research on CTLA-4 blockade.
Shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Tasuku Honjo.
ideas_zh: 改变免疫系统的调节方式为何能够产生抗肿瘤效应。
怎样用机制和临床分层解释疗效差异，而非只看平均结果。
ideas_en: Why changing immune regulation can generate an antitumor response.
How mechanisms and patient stratification help explain differences in treatment response.

people.name: 山中伸弥
people.bio_zh: 山中伸弥发现成熟细胞能够被重编程为诱导多能干细胞，改变了研究细胞命运和再生医学的方式，并获 2012 年诺贝尔奖。他持续推动 iPS 细胞的临床转化。值得学习的是如何把一个概念突破，逐步变成质量可控、来源稳定、能经受长期安全验证的细胞产品。
people.bio_en: Shinya Yamanaka is a stem-cell researcher whose work showed that mature cells can be reprogrammed into induced pluripotent stem cells. He shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with John Gurdon. Through Kyoto University and CiRA Foundation, he has worked on translating iPS technology into usable cell resources. His perspective connects biological reprogramming with manufacturing quality, clinical access and long-term safety.
people.current_zh: 京都大学 CiRA 教授及名誉主任、CiRA Foundation 理事长。
people.current_en: Professor and director emeritus of CiRA at Kyoto University; president of CiRA Foundation.
history_zh: 2006 年发表小鼠诱导多能干细胞研究，开启细胞重编程的重要路线。
获 2012 年诺贝尔奖；曾领导京都大学 CiRA，2022 年起为名誉主任。
history_en: Reported induced pluripotent stem cells in mice in 2006, opening a major route for cellular reprogramming.
Received the 2012 Nobel Prize; led Kyoto University's CiRA before becoming director emeritus in 2022.
ideas_zh: 细胞命运为何能够逆转，重编程成功又不代表所有功能都恢复。
临床级细胞资源需要怎样的制造标准和长期证据。
ideas_en: Why cell identity can be reprogrammed, and why this does not automatically restore every function.
What manufacturing standards and long-term evidence are required for clinical-grade cell resources.

His career includes leadership in academic research and at Roche's pharmaceutical research organization. He now continues work connected with the Hubrecht Institute and Utrecht University. His perspective is useful for evaluating disease models: what they faithfully capture, what they omit and how they inform treatment development.

people.current_en: Distinguished group leader at the Hubrecht Institute and professor at Utrecht University, researching organoids.

2022—2025 年领导 Roche 药物研究与早期开发部门。
history_en: Led the Hubrecht Institute and advanced adult stem-cell and organoid research.
Headed Roche Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development from 2022 to 2025.

学术中的发现标准与药企中的项目决策标准如何连接。

people.name: 邓宏魁
people.bio_zh: 邓宏魁长期研究细胞命运调控和化学重编程，推动用小分子改变细胞状态并探索再生医学应用。他的研究把机制发现、细胞制备和早期临床验证连接起来。适合关注怎样从原创底层方法走向疾病治疗，以及单例结果、临床可重复性和规模化生产之间的距离。
people.bio_en: Hongkui Deng is a stem-cell researcher at Peking University studying cell fate and chemical reprogramming. His work explores how small molecules can change cellular identity and generate cells relevant to regenerative medicine. His research trajectory connects a foundational laboratory method with manufacturing and early clinical translation. It provides a useful lens on the difference between an initial clinical result, reproducible treatment and a broadly usable therapeutic platform.
people.current_zh: 北京大学教授；化学重编程与再生医学研究者。
people.current_en: Professor at Peking University, working on chemical reprogramming and regenerative medicine.
history_zh: 曾在纽约大学从事博士后研究，并在 ViaCell 领导分子生物学研究。
2001 年加入北京大学，持续推进小分子细胞重编程与细胞治疗。
history_en: Undertook postdoctoral research at New York University and led molecular-biology research at ViaCell.
Joined Peking University in 2001 and advanced small-molecule reprogramming and cell-therapy research.

原创技术从细胞制备走向临床，需要跨过哪些验证环节。

Which validation steps connect an original cell-generation technology with clinical use.

people.bio_en: Robert Langer is an MIT Institute Professor whose work spans drug delivery, biomaterials and tissue engineering. He often starts with a practical medical limitation and asks what materials or engineering approach could overcome it. His laboratory has also helped create many biotechnology companies. His public conversations offer a detailed view of invention, interdisciplinary teams and the long path from a promising experiment to a manufacturable product.
people.current_zh: MIT David H. Koch Institute Professor；药物递送与生物材料研究者。
people.current_en: David H. Koch Institute Professor at MIT, researching drug delivery and biomaterials.
history_zh: 以聚合物控制药物释放等工作连接化学工程与医学。
长期参与组织工程和生物科技公司创建，包括 Moderna 的早期创立。
history_en: Connected chemical engineering with medicine through work including polymer-based controlled drug release.
Advanced tissue engineering and helped found biotechnology companies, including Moderna.
ideas_zh: 如何把一个临床瓶颈改写成能验证的工程问题。
团队、专利、制造与合作如何共同决定转化路径。
ideas_en: How to translate a clinical bottleneck into a testable engineering problem.
How teams, intellectual property, manufacturing and partnerships shape translation.

people.name: Katalin Karikó

people.bio_en: Katalin Karikó is a biochemist whose work with Drew Weissman on modified nucleosides helped make mRNA-based therapeutics practical. They received the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Her career spans academic research and work at BioNTech. Her account is valuable beyond perseverance: it explains how immune recognition, molecular stability and protein expression create interacting obstacles that must be solved before a platform becomes clinically useful.
people.current_zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学神经外科兼职教授；mRNA 生物化学研究者、BioNTech 前高级副总裁。
people.current_en: Adjunct professor of neurosurgery at the University of Pennsylvania; mRNA biochemist and former BioNTech senior vice president.
history_zh: 长期在宾夕法尼亚大学研究 RNA，并与 Drew Weissman 合作研究核苷修饰。
曾在 BioNTech 推动 mRNA 应用；与 Weissman 共获 2023 年诺贝尔奖。
history_en: Studied RNA for many years at Penn, collaborating with Drew Weissman on nucleoside modifications.
Advanced mRNA applications at BioNTech and shared the 2023 Nobel Prize with Weissman.
ideas_zh: mRNA 平台为什么必须同时解决免疫识别与有效表达。
如何用实验反馈维持长期研究，而不是只靠信念坚持。
ideas_en: Why mRNA platforms must address immune recognition and effective expression together.
How experimental feedback can guide a long research program beyond conviction alone.

people.name: Uğur Şahin
people.bio_zh: Uğur Şahin 是肿瘤免疫研究者和 BioNTech 联合创始人，将个体化治疗与技术平台结合。他的经历连接癌症研究、mRNA 和产品开发，适合学习科学路线如何成为产品路线，以及不同疾病之间能共享哪些能力、哪些条件不能直接复制。
people.bio_en: Uğur Şahin is an oncologist, immunology researcher and co-founder of BioNTech. His work connects personalized cancer treatment with platforms that can be adapted to different biological targets, including mRNA technologies. His experience is useful for understanding the transition from a scientific program to product development. A recurring question is which capabilities can be reused across diseases and which still require distinct clinical evidence and operational choices.
people.current_zh: BioNTech 联合创始人；肿瘤免疫、个体化治疗与 mRNA 技术研究者。
people.current_en: Co-founder of BioNTech and researcher in cancer immunology, personalized treatment and mRNA technologies.
history_zh: 在肿瘤免疫领域开展临床与基础研究，探索针对患者特点的治疗。
2008 年联合创立 BioNTech，推动 mRNA 平台及肿瘤治疗研发。
history_en: Conducted clinical and basic research in cancer immunology and patient-specific treatment strategies.
Co-founded BioNTech in 2008, advancing mRNA platforms and cancer-therapy development.
ideas_zh: 个体化治疗如何兼顾每位患者的差异与平台化制造。
技术平台在癌症和感染性疾病之间迁移时有哪些边界。
ideas_en: How personalized treatment can accommodate patient differences while using platform manufacturing.
Which limits matter when a technology moves between cancer and infectious disease.

people.name: Siddhartha Mukherjee
people.bio_zh: Mukherjee 是肿瘤科医生、研究者和医学作家，著有《众病之王》《基因传》和《细胞之歌》。他把癌症、基因与细胞治疗放进医学史和科学观念的变化中讨论，帮助理解一种疗法背后的疾病模型，以及新观察如何迫使研究者修改解释。
people.bio_en: Siddhartha Mukherjee is an oncologist, researcher and writer whose books include The Emperor of All Maladies, The Gene and The Song of the Cell. His conversations place biomedical advances within the history of changing scientific ideas. He is especially valuable for connecting observations in patients with models of cancer and cellular behavior, while explaining how new treatments expose gaps in what researchers thought they understood.
people.current_zh: 哥伦比亚大学肿瘤学研究者、临床医生与医学作家。
people.current_en: Oncology researcher at Columbia University, clinician and medical writer.
history_zh: 接受医学与肿瘤学训练，将临床工作与癌症机制研究结合。
《众病之王》获 2011 年普利策奖，随后出版关于基因和细胞的著作。
history_en: Trained in medicine and oncology, combining patient care with research into cancer mechanisms.
Won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for The Emperor of All Maladies and later wrote books on genes and cells.
ideas_zh: 疾病模型如何影响研究者选择观察什么和治疗什么。
如何把新疗法放入证据、历史与未解决问题的脉络。
ideas_en: How models of disease influence what researchers observe and try to treat.
How to place new therapies in the context of evidence, history and unresolved questions.

people.name: 杨璐菡
people.bio_zh: 杨璐菡是基因组工程研究者和启函生物创始人，早期参与多重基因编辑与异种器官移植相关研究，后扩展到通用型细胞治疗。她的经历适合观察复杂生物工程怎样走出实验室：不仅需要修改多个基因，还必须同时面对免疫相容性、产品制造和临床验证等相互影响的问题。
people.bio_en: Luhan Yang is a genome-engineering researcher and founder of Qihan Biotech. Her earlier work involved multiplex genome editing and the engineering challenges of xenotransplantation, followed by efforts in broadly compatible cell therapies. Her trajectory is useful for examining how complex biological engineering moves toward clinical products. Editing multiple genes is only one part of a problem that also involves immune compatibility, manufacturing consistency and carefully staged clinical testing.
people.current_zh: 启函生物创始人兼 CEO；基因编辑与细胞治疗研究者。
people.current_en: Founder and CEO of Qihan Biotech, working on genome editing and cell therapy.
history_zh: 在北京大学与哈佛接受训练，参与大规模基因编辑与猪基因组工程研究。
联合创办 eGenesis，后创立启函生物，推进免疫相容性与细胞疗法。
history_en: Trained at Peking University and Harvard, contributing to large-scale genome editing and pig-genome engineering.
Co-founded eGenesis and later founded Qihan Biotech to advance immune compatibility and cell therapies.
ideas_zh: 怎样管理多重基因工程中互相制约的设计目标。
异种移植与通用细胞治疗共享哪些工具，又有哪些不同风险。
ideas_en: How to manage interacting design goals in multiplex genome engineering.
Which tools xenotransplantation and universal cell therapies share, and where their challenges differ.

people.name: Drew Endy
people.bio_zh: Drew Endy 是合成生物学的重要推动者，关注怎样让生物工程拥有更可靠的工具、标准和协作方式。他不仅讨论药物，也思考材料、制造、环境与未来经济。其访谈适合从单个项目退后一步，理解通用基础设施和开放工具为何可能决定整个领域的能力边界。
people.bio_en: Drew Endy is a Stanford bioengineer and an early architect of synthetic biology. He asks how biology can become easier to engineer through better standards, tools, measurement and collaboration. His interests extend beyond medicine into manufacturing, materials and the organization of a bioeconomy. His public talks are useful for understanding why improvements to shared infrastructure can matter more broadly than any single biological product.
people.current_zh: 斯坦福大学生物工程副教授；合成生物学与生物制造研究者。
people.current_en: Associate professor of bioengineering at Stanford University, working on synthetic biology and biomanufacturing.
history_zh: 早期参与 MIT 合成生物学教学和研究，推动标准生物部件与开放工具。
参与建立 iGEM、BioBricks 等社区与基础设施，后在斯坦福持续研究。
history_en: Helped develop synthetic-biology education and research at MIT, including standardized biological parts and open tools.
Helped build communities and infrastructure including iGEM and BioBricks, continuing his work at Stanford.
ideas_zh: 怎样把生物工程从反复试错推进为更可靠的设计过程。
测量、标准与开放工具如何影响材料和制造应用的成本。
ideas_en: How biological engineering can become a more reliable design process.
How measurement, standards and open tools affect the economics of materials and manufacturing.

people.name: Frances Arnold
people.bio_zh: Frances Arnold 将定向进化发展为改造酶的重要方法，获诺贝尔化学奖。她利用变异、筛选和迭代处理人类难以完全理解的复杂分子系统。这不仅适用于药物和绿色化学，也为思考 AI 设计、实验筛选与现实反馈的关系提供案例。
people.bio_en: Frances Arnold is a Caltech chemical engineer who pioneered directed evolution as a practical method for improving enzymes. She received the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for that work. Her approach uses variation and selection to solve problems that are difficult to design from complete mechanistic knowledge. It offers a concrete framework for thinking about iteration, experimental feedback and the relationship between computational proposals and useful molecular performance.
people.current_zh: 加州理工学院 Linus Pauling 教授；定向进化与酶工程研究者。
people.current_en: Linus Pauling Professor at Caltech, researching directed evolution and enzyme engineering.
history_zh: 在加州理工学院发展通过变异与筛选优化酶的研究路线。
因酶的定向进化获得 2018 年诺贝尔化学奖，并推动相关工业应用。
history_en: Developed methods at Caltech for optimizing enzymes through variation and selection.
Received the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for directed evolution of enzymes and advanced industrial applications.
ideas_zh: 当系统过于复杂时，怎样设计有效的筛选与迭代过程。
计算设计与实验进化怎样互相补足。
ideas_en: How to design effective selection and iteration when a system is too complex to model fully.
How computational design and experimental evolution can complement each other.

people.name: Jay Keasling
people.bio_zh: Jay Keasling 是代谢工程和生物制造研究者，利用微生物合成药物原料、燃料和化学品。他的重要价值在于把细胞内部的代谢设计与工业生产的现实相连接。适合学习怎样组合酶和代谢通路，也适合理解为什么实验室产物能够做出来，并不意味着能在市场上以合适成本供应。
people.bio_en: Jay Keasling is a metabolic engineer who develops microbes to produce useful chemicals, fuels and pharmaceutical ingredients. His work at Berkeley and the Joint BioEnergy Institute connects pathway design with the practical demands of biological manufacturing. He is especially useful for understanding the gap between demonstrating a biosynthetic route and making it economically useful. Yield, productivity, feedstocks, recovery and demand all influence whether a process succeeds.
people.current_zh: 加州大学伯克利分校教授、Joint BioEnergy Institute CEO；代谢工程研究者。
people.current_en: Professor at UC Berkeley and CEO of the Joint BioEnergy Institute, working on metabolic engineering.
history_zh: 推动合成生物学与代谢工程工具，用微生物制造复杂分子。
参与青蒿素前体生物合成路线，并长期研究生物燃料与化学品制造。
history_en: Advanced synthetic-biology and metabolic-engineering tools for producing complex molecules in microbes.
Contributed to biosynthetic production of an artemisinin precursor and pursued research on biofuels and chemicals.
ideas_zh: 细胞内部的通路优化怎样受到宿主生理和资源分配限制。
产率、产量、生产速度与分离成本如何影响工业可行性。
ideas_en: How host physiology and resource allocation constrain metabolic-pathway optimization.
How yield, titer, productivity and separation costs affect industrial feasibility.

people.name: James J. Collins

people.bio_en: James J. Collins is an MIT bioengineer and a founder of synthetic biology. His work spans engineered gene circuits, diagnostics and the use of machine learning to identify antibiotic candidates. He combines an engineering perspective with attention to specific biomedical problems. His research is useful for understanding how a compelling computational result is connected to biological testing, practical deployment and the problem of antimicrobial resistance.

people.current_en: Termeer Professor of Medical Engineering and Science at MIT and a member of the Broad Institute.
history_zh: 参与建立合成生物学领域，开发可控制细胞行为的基因回路。
推动合成生物学诊断及 AI 抗生素研究，并参与创立 Phare Bio。
history_en: Helped establish synthetic biology through engineered circuits that control cellular behavior.
Advanced synthetic-biology diagnostics and AI-driven antibiotic research, helping found Phare Bio.

AI 找到的抗菌分子需要通过哪些实验才能成为候选药物。

Which experiments connect an AI-identified antibacterial molecule with a drug-development candidate.

people.bio_en: Christina Smolke is a synthetic biologist and co-founder of Antheia, which develops microbial production routes for complex pharmaceutical ingredients. Her work spans RNA engineering and the reconstruction of plant-derived chemistry in engineered organisms. She offers a useful perspective on changing pharmaceutical supply chains through biology. A successful pathway must also become a reliable process with consistent quality, robust scale-up and an economically meaningful place in manufacturing.

people.current_en: Co-founder and CEO of Antheia and adjunct professor at Stanford University.

联合创办 Antheia，将复杂药用分子的微生物合成推进到制造应用。
history_en: Conducted RNA-engineering and synthetic-biology research at Caltech and Stanford.
Co-founded Antheia to translate microbial synthesis of complex pharmaceutical ingredients into manufacturing.

原料药生物制造如何改变供应链，并满足稳定性与质量要求。

How biological manufacturing can reshape pharmaceutical supply chains while meeting quality requirements.

people.bio_zh: 陈国强是清华大学微生物与生物材料研究者，长期研究聚羟基脂肪酸酯等可生物降解材料，以及降低发酵生产成本的方法。他的工作特别贴合医学之外的生物经济兴趣，能够帮助理解环保材料如何同时满足性能、生产成本和使用场景要求。此处指清华 PHA 研究者。
people.bio_en: Guo-Qiang Chen is a Tsinghua University researcher working on microbial biotechnology and polyhydroxyalkanoates, a family of biodegradable polymers. His work connects engineered microbes with materials and manufacturing processes. He is particularly relevant for exploring biotechnology beyond medicine, including how material performance, fermentation conditions and production costs interact. This profile refers to the Tsinghua PHA researcher, rather than other public figures with the same Chinese name.

推进 PHA 材料和下一代工业生物技术，探索更低成本的发酵路线。
history_en: Joined Tsinghua University in 1994 and pursued microbial physiology and engineering.
Advanced PHA materials and next-generation industrial biotechnology, including lower-cost fermentation approaches.
ideas_zh: 可降解材料的分子结构怎样决定加工与使用性能。
耐受型底盘和开放发酵如何影响生物制造成本。
ideas_en: How the molecular structure of biodegradable materials affects processing and performance.
How robust microbial hosts and open fermentation influence manufacturing costs.

people.name: Matt Kaeberlein

people.bio_en: Matt Kaeberlein is an aging biologist and co-founder of the Dog Aging Project. His research examines mechanisms and interventions that influence lifespan and healthspan, with particular interest in translating laboratory findings into more informative studies. He often discusses the limits of evidence behind popular longevity claims. His work connects human health, companion-animal medicine and the practical challenge of measuring meaningful benefits rather than promising biomarker changes.
people.current_zh: 衰老生物学家、Dog Aging Project 联合创始人；曾任华盛顿大学教授。
people.current_en: Aging biologist and co-founder of the Dog Aging Project; formerly a professor at the University of Washington.
history_zh: 曾在华盛顿大学研究衰老机制及寿命干预，参与建立 Dog Aging Project。
后来参与创建并领导 Optispan；2026 年访谈中说明已离开其 CEO 岗位。
history_en: Studied aging mechanisms and lifespan interventions at the University of Washington and helped establish the Dog Aging Project.
Later co-founded and led Optispan; in a 2026 interview he said he had left its CEO role.
ideas_zh: 从酵母、小鼠到犬和人，哪些证据可以迁移，哪些不能。
怎样区分延长寿命、改善健康与改变一个测量指标。
ideas_en: Which findings can transfer from yeast and mice to dogs and humans, and which cannot.
How to distinguish lifespan extension, health improvement and changes in a measured biomarker.

people.name: Vadim Gladyshev
people.bio_zh: Vadim Gladyshev 研究衰老的分子机制、跨物种寿命差异以及生物年龄的测量。他把比较生物学、组学和实验干预结合，用多种视角追问生命为何衰老。其讨论适合帮助区分描述性规律、机制解释和干预效果，也能避免把某个年龄指标下降直接当成健康改善。
people.bio_en: Vadim Gladyshev is a Harvard-affiliated biologist studying aging, longevity and molecular processes that differ across species. His research combines comparative biology, large-scale measurements and experimental interventions. He is useful for exploring what aging means as a biological process rather than a single clinical condition. A recurring distinction is between observing an age-associated pattern, explaining its mechanism and showing that changing it produces a meaningful benefit.
people.current_zh: 哈佛医学院教授、Brigham and Women's Hospital 研究者；研究衰老与氧化还原生物学。
people.current_en: Professor at Harvard Medical School and researcher at Brigham and Women's Hospital, studying aging and redox biology.
history_zh: 早期研究硒蛋白与氧化还原机制，逐步拓展到寿命和衰老。
运用跨物种比较、组学和生物年龄指标研究衰老及年轻化。
history_en: Studied selenoproteins and redox biology before expanding into longevity and aging.
Uses cross-species comparisons, omics and biological-age measurements to investigate aging and rejuvenation.
ideas_zh: 跨物种比较怎样帮助发现衰老中更普遍的机制。
如何区分衰老的测量工具、解释模型和有效干预。
ideas_en: How comparisons across species help identify more general mechanisms of aging.
How to distinguish aging measurements, explanatory models and effective interventions.

people.name: Tony Wyss-Coray
people.bio_zh: Tony Wyss-Coray 研究大脑衰老、阿尔茨海默病与血液中的全身信号，探索身体其他部位怎样影响脑功能。他的工作把神经科学与系统性衰老联系起来，适合学习如何由动物实验发现候选机制，再逐步设计可验证的人体研究，而不是把早期现象直接理解为成熟的年轻化疗法。
people.bio_en: Tony Wyss-Coray is a Stanford neuroscientist studying brain aging and neurodegeneration. His laboratory investigates how signals circulating through the body influence brain structure and function. The work connects neuroscience with systemic aging and the search for therapeutic mechanisms. He is useful for understanding how animal experiments generate hypotheses, how those hypotheses can be tested in humans and why an intriguing biological effect is not yet an established rejuvenation treatment.
people.current_zh: 斯坦福大学神经学教授、Knight Initiative for Brain Resilience 主任。
people.current_en: Professor of neurology at Stanford and director of the Knight Initiative for Brain Resilience.
history_zh: 长期研究阿尔茨海默病、认知老化和免疫信号。
团队揭示循环血液因子能够影响脑功能，并推进相关机制研究。
history_en: Has investigated Alzheimer's disease, cognitive aging and immune signaling.
His team showed that circulating blood factors can influence brain function and pursued the underlying mechanisms.
ideas_zh: 身体其他器官如何通过循环信号改变大脑状态。
从动物效应到人体治疗，需要怎样的机制和试验证据。
ideas_en: How other organs influence the brain through circulating signals.
What mechanistic and clinical evidence connects an animal effect with a human treatment.

people.name: Steve Horvath
people.bio_zh: Steve Horvath 是表观遗传时钟的重要研究者，利用 DNA 甲基化等数据估计生物年龄并研究衰老。他的工作让衰老测量更具可操作性，也带来新的解释问题。适合学习一个预测指标如何建立与验证，以及为什么指标变年轻、风险下降和实际健康收益是需要分别证明的命题。
people.bio_en: Steve Horvath is a researcher known for developing epigenetic clocks that estimate age from DNA methylation patterns. He returned to UCLA in 2026 after working at Altos Labs. His work makes aging measurable in new ways while raising important questions about interpretation. He is especially useful for distinguishing a predictive biomarker from a biological mechanism and for asking when changing a clock actually signals improved health.
people.current_zh: UCLA 医学教授、衰老生物学研究主任；表观遗传时钟研究者。
people.current_en: Professor of Medicine and Director of Aging Biology Research at UCLA.
history_zh: 在 UCLA 开发表观遗传年龄估计方法，包括跨组织 DNA 甲基化时钟。
曾在 Altos Labs 工作，2026 年 7 月回到 UCLA 建立研究团队。
history_en: Developed epigenetic-age estimation methods at UCLA, including a multi-tissue DNA-methylation clock.
Worked at Altos Labs before returning to UCLA to establish his laboratory in July 2026.
ideas_zh: 一个衰老时钟如何训练、验证，并避免数据和人群偏差。
指标改变何时可以代表疾病风险或健康寿命的改变。
ideas_en: How an aging clock is trained and validated while accounting for population and data biases.
When a change in a biomarker can indicate a change in disease risk or healthspan.

people.name: 王晓东（细胞凋亡）
people.bio_zh: 王晓东是细胞死亡研究的重要科学家，研究细胞凋亡的分子机制，并参与生物医药创业。他的经历把基础生化实验、疾病理解和药物发现连接起来，适合学习如何从一个细胞过程寻找可干预环节，以及为什么深刻机制认识仍需要经过药物性质和临床效果的多重检验。
people.bio_en: Xiaodong Wang is a biochemist known for elucidating central mechanisms of programmed cell death. His work has connected fundamental studies of apoptosis and related pathways with opportunities for drug discovery. He has also helped build research institutions and biotechnology companies, including BeiGene. His perspective is useful for understanding how a detailed molecular mechanism becomes a therapeutic hypothesis and why that hypothesis still requires extensive pharmacological and clinical testing.
people.current_zh: 北京生命科学研究所研究者；细胞死亡与药物发现领域科学家、百济神州联合创始人。
people.current_en: Researcher at the National Institute of Biological Sciences, Beijing; cell-death scientist and co-founder of BeiGene.
history_zh: 早期在美国开展细胞凋亡研究，揭示细胞色素 c 等关键分子的作用。
参与建立北京生命科学研究所，并将细胞死亡机制研究延伸至药物发现。
history_en: Conducted apoptosis research in the United States, clarifying roles for cytochrome c and other key molecules.
Helped establish NIBS in Beijing and extended cell-death research toward drug discovery.
ideas_zh: 怎样通过生化拆解找到细胞过程中的关键因果环节。
从机制靶点到药物，需要解决哪些与基础研究不同的问题。
ideas_en: How biochemical dissection identifies causal steps within a cellular process.
Which additional problems arise when moving from a mechanistic target to a drug.

people.name: 李文辉
people.bio_zh: 李文辉研究病毒进入细胞的机制，因发现乙肝和丁肝病毒受体 NTCP 而广为人知。他的研究是基础发现指导应用的直接例子：确认病毒借助什么进入细胞，会改变疾病模型、感染实验和药物开发路线。适合学习如何长期攻克一个清晰而困难的问题，并判断发现之后真正打开了哪些机会。
people.bio_en: Wenhui Li is a virologist known for identifying NTCP as a functional receptor for hepatitis B and D viruses. His research shows how a basic mechanistic discovery can change experimental models and therapeutic strategies. Work on viral entry provides a direct connection between molecular interactions and disease intervention. He is valuable for understanding how a focused, difficult biological question can open several downstream routes for research and drug development.
people.current_zh: 北京生命科学研究所研究员、清华大学相关研究平台教授；病毒受体研究者。
people.current_en: Investigator at NIBS, Beijing, and professor associated with Tsinghua's biomedical research programs, studying viral receptors.
history_zh: 在北京协和医学院获得博士学位，随后在哈佛从事病毒入侵机制研究。
团队发现乙肝和丁肝病毒的 NTCP 受体，获 2022 年未来科学大奖。
history_en: Received his doctorate from Peking Union Medical College and studied viral entry at Harvard.
His team identified NTCP as a receptor for hepatitis B and D viruses; he received the 2022 Future Science Prize.
ideas_zh: 受体发现怎样改变疾病模型与可进行的实验。
怎样从病毒入侵机制找到治疗路线，并检验其局限。
ideas_en: How identifying a receptor changes disease models and available experiments.
How viral-entry mechanisms suggest treatment strategies and reveal their limits.

people.name: Eric Topol
people.bio_zh: Eric Topol 是心脏病学家、临床研究者和作家，讨论基因组学、数字医疗与 AI 如何影响患者照护。他持续写作并采访科学家，适合将分散的医学进展组织成系统认识，重点判断技术表现是否转化为患者获益，以及医疗流程是否改善。
people.bio_en: Eric Topol is a cardiologist, clinical researcher and medical writer at Scripps Research. His work spans genomics, digital medicine and artificial intelligence in healthcare. Through books, essays and interviews, he connects emerging technologies with clinical evidence and patient experience. He is especially useful for evaluating whether impressive technical performance changes outcomes, improves care delivery or simply creates another measurement without a demonstrated benefit.
people.current_zh: Scripps Research 执行副总裁、Scripps Research Translational Institute 创始主任。
people.current_en: Executive vice president of Scripps Research and founding director of its Translational Institute.
history_zh: 长期开展心血管临床研究，并推进遗传学与个体化医学。
2007 年创办 Scripps 转化研究机构，持续撰写 Ground Truths 与医学著作。
history_en: Conducted cardiovascular clinical research and advanced genetics and individualized medicine.
Founded the Scripps translational research institute in 2007 and writes Ground Truths and books on medicine.
ideas_zh: 怎样判断 AI 医疗的实验指标是否转化为患者实际获益。
临床流程、医生时间与医患关系如何影响技术价值。
ideas_en: How to assess whether AI performance metrics translate into benefits for patients.
How care workflows, clinicians' time and patient relationships shape a technology's value.

people.name: Jason Kelly
people.bio_zh: Jason Kelly 是 Ginkgo Bioworks 联合创始人，从经营视角讨论细胞编程平台和生物制造。他适合补充产业观察：通用工具怎样成为客户愿意付费的服务，自动化能否改善研发经济性。阅读时可分别考察公司愿景、技术能力与商业结果。
people.bio_en: Jason Kelly is a co-founder and CEO of Ginkgo Bioworks, a company developing tools and services for biological engineering. He brings an operating perspective to synthetic biology: how automation, shared infrastructure and platform capabilities might change the economics of research. His conversations are useful for evaluating the relationship between a compelling technical vision and customer demand, organizational execution and the financial performance of a business.

people.current_en: Co-founder and CEO of Ginkgo Bioworks, offering an operating perspective on synthetic biology.

推动面向不同客户和应用的细胞工程平台，并拓展自动化工具与服务。
history_en: Trained in biological engineering at MIT and co-founded Ginkgo Bioworks in 2008.
Developed a cell-engineering platform serving multiple applications and expanded automation tools and services.
ideas_zh: 通用生物平台需要怎样的客户需求才能成立。
如何用项目复用、产出与单位成本检验平台规模效应。
ideas_en: What kinds of customer demand can support a general-purpose biological platform.
How reuse, useful output and unit costs can test claims about platform scale.

people.bio_en: Emily Leproust is a chemist and co-founder of Twist Bioscience, which develops high-throughput DNA synthesis technologies and related products. She offers an infrastructure perspective on biotechnology: how changes in the cost and reliability of writing DNA affect downstream research. Her discussions are useful for understanding applications in protein engineering, drug discovery and data storage, while separating technological capability from manufacturing execution and commercial demand.
people.current_zh: Twist Bioscience 联合创始人兼 CEO；DNA 合成技术企业家。
people.current_en: Co-founder and CEO of Twist Bioscience, focused on DNA-synthesis technology.
history_zh: 接受有机化学训练，并在产业界从事 DNA 合成技术开发。
联合创办 Twist Bioscience，推动基于硅芯片的高通量 DNA 合成平台。
history_en: Trained in organic chemistry and worked on DNA-synthesis technology in industry.
Co-founded Twist Bioscience and advanced a silicon-based platform for high-throughput DNA synthesis.

平台制造中的错误率、规模与客户工作流怎样共同决定价值。

How error rates, scale and customers' workflows jointly determine manufacturing-platform value.

people.bio_en: Noubar Afeyan is a biochemical engineer, entrepreneur and investor who founded Flagship Pioneering and helped create Moderna. His approach emphasizes generating ambitious scientific hypotheses, testing them and building companies around those that become credible. He is useful for understanding the organization of early biotechnology innovation: how teams explore uncertainty, how platforms differ from individual products and how research decisions evolve as evidence accumulates.
people.current_zh: Flagship Pioneering 创始人兼 CEO、Moderna 联合创始人及董事长。
people.current_en: Founder and CEO of Flagship Pioneering; co-founder and chairman of Moderna.
history_zh: 在 MIT 获得生物化学工程博士学位，随后多次参与创办技术企业。
2000 年创办 Flagship Pioneering，并参与创建 Moderna 等生物科技公司。
history_en: Earned a doctorate in biochemical engineering at MIT and subsequently helped build technology companies.
Founded Flagship Pioneering in 2000 and helped create biotechnology companies including Moderna.
ideas_zh: 怎样把一个尚无充分证据的技术假设组织成可检验计划。
平台、产品和公司的边界如何随着证据变化而调整。
ideas_en: How to turn an uncertain technological hypothesis into a testable research program.
How the boundaries between a platform, a product and a company evolve with evidence.

people.name: Michael Mauboussin
people.bio_zh: Counterpoint Global研究负责人、作者和教师，长期把概率、心理学与复杂系统用于投资判断。他的研究重视基本概率、预期差、竞争优势以及运气与能力的区分，适合训练通用的思考方法，避免仅凭精彩故事或一次结果判断一个观点。
people.bio_en: Michael Mauboussin leads consilient research at Counterpoint Global and is an author and longtime Columbia Business School teacher. His work brings probability, psychology, and complex-systems thinking into investing. He is particularly useful for learning how to distinguish skill from luck, compare outcomes with prior expectations, and evaluate competitive advantage without allowing a persuasive narrative or a single result to substitute for careful reasoning.

ideas_en: Distinguishing good luck, skill, and a reliable decision process.
Using base rates and market expectations to assess opportunities.

people.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
people.bio_zh: 长期宏观投资人，创办Duquesne，并有管理Soros投资组合的经历。他的访谈常讨论流动性、周期、集中判断与及时认错，尤其强调事实变化后的行动。适合学习如何在强烈观点和可修正性之间保持平衡，而不把预测当成身份。
people.bio_en: Stanley Druckenmiller is a macro investor who founded Duquesne and previously worked with George Soros. He now invests through his family office. His interviews examine liquidity, economic cycles, concentrated judgment, and the willingness to change course quickly. He is useful for understanding how strong conviction can coexist with flexibility, and why responding to changing evidence matters more than defending an earlier forecast.

people.name: Ray Dalio
people.bio_zh: Bridgewater创始人、作者和长期宏观研究者。他把债务、货币、制度与历史周期组织成解释框架，也分享决策和组织原则。其内容适合建立宏观问题的系统地图，再用数据与不同历史案例检验框架的适用范围及局限。
people.bio_en: Ray Dalio founded Bridgewater Associates and writes about economic history, debt cycles, decision-making, and organizational principles. His public work organizes monetary and institutional change into broad explanatory frameworks. He is useful for developing a systematic map of macroeconomic questions, while comparing those frameworks with data and historical cases to understand both their explanatory power and the limits of any recurring-cycle analogy.

history_en: Founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975.

ideas_zh: 从债务、货币与制度理解宏观变化。
把原则当成可与现实对照的假设，而非固定答案。
ideas_en: Understanding macroeconomic change through debt, money, and institutions.
Treating principles as hypotheses to compare with reality rather than fixed answers.
